Joker: Folie a Deux Review: Da Vinci pissing on the Mona Lisa ____________________________________________ "Arthur Fleck is dead.       Long live the Joker." ____________________________________________ 👍: Soundtrack/Sounds: 10/10 Plot/Concept: 6.2/10 Pacing: 7.1/10 Characters: 6.3/10 Emotion: 7.2/10 Cinematography: 10/10 Casting: 9/10 Acting: 9.5/10 Ending: 9.3/10 Overall: 🍿74/90🍿 Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot more good things than people give it credit for. Joaquin Phoenix gives another incredible performance and carries every scene with intensity. I also enjoyed all of the songs , and the soundtrack and sound design create a unique mood. The visuals are beautiful , with grey but yet bright colours that make Gotham look perfect. The scene where Two-Face is born was one of my favourites . And the overall court sequence is excellent. I also liked the ending . I know most people hate it, but I thought it fit the story well. In my opinion, this film is still very overhated. The Message: Joker: Folie à Deux shows how society can turn a broken person into a symbol they never wanted to become. Arthur is no longer seen as a human being with fears, but as the Joker , an idea that people project their own anger onto. The film questions whether people truly care about justice or if they simply enjoy watching chaos. Do we become who we really are or who everyone expects us to be. Arthur struggles between being himself and living up to the Joker . The ending suggests that ideas can survive even when the people cannot. symbols are often more powerful than people, and once society creates a legend , it becomes almost impossible to forget, no matter how much someone changes. ____________________________________________ 👎: Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot of problems. The biggest one is that almost nothing happens. The story barely moves forward , and around 70% of the film feels wasted because there is almost no real progress from beginning to end. The direction is bland, and the overall screenplay is weak. I enjoyed the songs themselves, but the musical numbers often don't fit the story and become exhausting after a while. Good music alone isn't enough to carry such a thin plot. Harley Quinn was also disappointing because she barely does anything important. She had a lot of potential , but the screenplay gives her very little to give , making her feel completely unnecessary. I know the film is overhated , but it's still a pretty mid film . To make things even worse, I watched it at 2 a.m. , so I even lost sleep for it. ____________________________________________ Overall: Joker: Folie à Deux is a weak ass film , but it's still massively overhated. It has some genuinely great aspects , especially the acting, visuals, and music, but they're overshadowed by an unfocused story, bland direction, and wasted potential. The flaws are simply much bigger than the strengths, making it an average experience. Rating by Greatness: ⭐✨ Rating: ⭐⭐ ```````````````

Coringa: Delírio a Dois foi um filme de interpretação dúbia. Não é uma obra que odiei, muito pelo contrário, minhas expectativas eram extremamente altas por gostar muito do personagem Coringa, e talvez tenha sido justamente isso que tornou a decepção maior. Gosto da proposta do diretor de explorar o Arthur Fleck, aprofundando seus conflitos internos e mostrando o ser humano por trás do símbolo. As reflexões sobre identidade, solidão, julgamento e a forma como a sociedade constrói e destrói figuras públicas são interessantes e, em muitos momentos, muito bem executadas, o problema é que essa proposta entra em conflito com aquilo que o próprio filme promete, pois ao assistir a uma continuação de Coringa, é natural esperar o desenvolvimento do personagem que conhecemos, mas a narrativa permanece centrada quase exclusivamente em Arthur. Para outro filme, essa abordagem talvez funcionasse ainda melhor, mas, para uma sequência de Coringa, ela me pareceu uma escolha equivocada. Outro ponto que prejudicou bastante minha experiência foi o excesso de números musicais, que em diversos momentos tornaram o filme cansativo e quebraram completamente o ritmo da narrativa. Por fim, o desfecho também me dividiu, embora eu compreenda a intenção simbólica do diretor, a forma como Arthur morre me pareceu simples demais para um personagem tão marcante, portanto esperava um encerramento que desse mais grandeza à sua trajetória, e não um fim causado por alguém praticamente irrelevante para toda a construção da história. Ainda assim, reconheço que é um filme corajoso por fugir do convencional e propor discussões interessantes, minha decepção não veio da qualidade das reflexões, mas da sensação de que elas pertenciam a um filme sobre Arthur Fleck, e não à continuação do Coringa que eu esperava.

Após o primeiro filme, o qual continua glorioso em contar uma ótima história com os personagens da DC. A continuação tinha um enorme desafio, como manter a qualidade? Coringa 2 é um filme que não consegue se sustentar sozinho. Ele vive inteiramente à sombra do primeiro. A nova proposta de transformar a narrativa em um musical é, na teoria, interessante. Ela até combina com a leitura psicológica e frágil que esse universo fez do Coringa. O problema é que, na prática, a execução falha completamente. O longa não consegue decidir o que quer ser. Ele não funciona como musical, porque as músicas não impulsionam a história nem revelam nada novo sobre os personagens. E também não funciona como um drama de tribunal, porque o roteiro jurídico é fraco, arrastado e não constrói tensão real. No fim das contas, o que resta são dois pilares: as atuações, que continuam sendo impecáveis, especialmente de Joaquin Phoenix e Lady Gaga, e a fotografia, que segue linda e atmosférica. Mas tirando isso, o filme se esvazia. Não sobra substância, não sobra tema, não sobra impacto. Me parece que Todd Phillips gastou o filme inteiro tentando responder aos fãs que idolatraram o primeiro Coringa e transformaram aquele personagem em um ícone a ser seguido. Ele quis dizer: "olha, esse cara não é um símbolo, ele é só um doente". E tudo bem querer desconstruir isso. O problema é a forma. Ele mesmo criou essa versão do Coringa. Ele mesmo construiu um protagonista magnético, caótico e sedutor no primeiro filme. E agora parece arrependido disso. Em vez de aprofundar ou amadurecer essa ideia, ele optou pelo caminho mais raso e mais medíocre: desconstruir por desconstruir, chocar por chocar. O resultado é um filme que trai a própria proposta que o consagrou.

La elección del género musical para esta entrega creo que tenía mucho potencial. La forma en que los números musicales se integran a la cinta, como una representación de la locura dentro de la mente del Joker, funciona bastante bien. Sin embargo, la falta de un guion sólido termina afectando considerablemente esta decisión de género. En general, es una película que, si nunca hubiera existido, no habría pasado absolutamente nada. Incluso creo que mucha gente habría preferido que jamás se hiciera antes que ver cómo fueron desdibujando poco a poco todo lo que construyeron con tanta fuerza en la primera. Aun así, rescato su banda sonora y una fotografía muy cuidada e inteligentemente realizada. Visto En HBO Max

i think joker: folie à deux is one of the most misunderstood movies in recent years. before anything, i am NOT justifying arthur fleck’s actions. this man literally killed 6 people. understanding a character’s psychology does not mean excusing what they did. that’s what makes this movie so interesting to me. it isn’t asking us to forgive arthur, it’s asking us to watch him completely lose himself. the musical aspect was definitely a choice, and i understand why it didn’t work for everyone, but i think people missed what it was trying to do. i don’t think most of the singing is actually happening. i think it’s all inside arthur’s head. the songs are his fantasies, his escape, and another sign that he can no longer separate reality from the world he created. the movie isn’t about the rise of the joker. it’s about the death of arthur fleck. after the first movie, everyone wanted arthur to become the joker we know from the comics. the mastermind, the villain, the legend. but todd phillips almost feels like he’s challenging the audience by refusing to give us that. we wanted the myth of joker, but he keeps showing us the broken man underneath the makeup. and honestly, i think that’s the point. gotham didn’t love arthur. they loved joker. harley didn’t fall in love with arthur fleck, she fell in love with the idea of joker. everyone was obsessed with the fantasy, including the audience. lady gaga was also incredible. i just wish we got more of her as harley quinn because she can genuinely act her ass off. but maybe the reason we don’t fully understand harley is because arthur doesn’t fully understand her either. we only see the version of her that exists in his mind. this movie is messy, and i understand why people don’t connect with it, but i think there is so much more going on underneath the surface. the musical numbers, the courtroom, the relationship with harley, and the ending all feel like a reflection of arthur’s collapsing mind. not a perfect movie, but definitely a much deeper one than people give it credit for.

Todd Philipps et sa réinterprétation du mythe du Joker ont surpris bien du monde en remportant le Lion d'or à Venise en 2019. La barre était haute pour cette suite, la bien nommée Folie à deux. Le réalisateur a eu la bonne idée de s'en aller ailleurs, entre drame psychologique, musical, film de procès et tragédie. Le résultat ne remplit pas toutes ses promesses et risque d'en désorienter plus d'un. Un deuxième tome, donc. Faut-il avoir vu le premier? Ce n'est pas absolument un prérequis (même si ça aide). Car nous retrouvons Arthur Fleck (Joaquin Phoenix), deux ans après les cinq meurtres commis par son alter ego, Joker. Il croupit à l'hôpital psychiatrique d'Arkham, la peau sur les os, aux mains de gardiens cruels et violents. Les tortures psychologiques et physiques se poursuivent… La même violence qui a fait basculer Arthur dans la folie psychotique du Joker. Sauf qu'il est tellement assommé de médicaments que son double maléfique reste tapi dans l'ombre! En attente de son procès, il va rencontrer Harleen «Lee» Quinzel (Lady Gaga), qui séjourne dans l'aile minimale après avoir mis le feu à la maison de ses parents. Ils vont peu à peu tomber follement amoureux. Cette soudaine passion ne fait pas le bonheur de son avocate (Catherine Keener) — les deux femmes ont une vision opposée d'Arthur/Joker… La Harley Quinn en devenir s'éloigne du canon de DC Comics pour apparaître plus manipulatrice et amorale. Déjà dans le premier long métrage, la mise en scène de Philipps consistait à filmer l'action du point de vue d'Arthur en jouant sur la réalité et ses illusions. Dans Folie à deux, il pousse le concept plus loin. Le monde parallèle du Joker prend la forme de morceaux musicaux parfois baroques (avec de superbes éclairages), parfois plus terre à terre. L'interprétation de Close to You des Carpenters par Lady Gaga s'avère un petit moment d'anthologie. La chanteuse livre de superbes performances en reprenant des classiques de l'âge d'or de la comédie musicale. Ce qui ne laissera aucun spectateur indifférent. En fait, l'ensemble de Folie à deux risque de profondément diviser. Philipps et son scénariste, Scott Silver, voulaient manifestement ne pas refaire le même Joker et pousser au bout la logique de briser le moule des films de superhéros. Le personnage même est l'ombre de ce qu'il était — son rire dément, déclenché par le stress et nourri par ses traumas, ne résonne presque plus… Il faut dire qu'outre les moments à l'asile, filmé avec une esthétique glauque, et les saynètes musicales, l'essentiel du long métrage se déroule au palais de justice. À cet endroit, Philipps filme le procès comme une téléréalité, dénonçant l'obscène voyeurisme et la recherche de sensationnalisme d'une société malade et polarisée — oui, c'est une allusion claire à la société états-unienne actuelle. Joker va mettre le feu aux poudres! Dans ce mélange stylistique et d'exploration thématique, Philipps trop embrasse et mal étreint. Cette forme éclatée marque cependant une volonté d'offrir du cinéma autrement, loin des standards hollywoodiens — ce qui ne l'empêche pas d'être miné par des longueurs. Mais si on s'attarde au propos, plus le film avance, et plus le spectateur comprend à quel point le clown est triste. C'est au cœur de cette implacable progression que loge la tragédie. Arthur révèle à quel point la société l'a broyé et qu'elle ferme les yeux sur ses problèmes de santé mentale. Joker: Folie à deux est un long métrage sombre, certains diront nihiliste (en phase avec son époque?). Le spectateur y puisera ce qu'il veut bien. Ou pas. Mais personne ne contestera que Phoenix y livre encore une performance totalement incarnée (oui, comme celle qui lui a valu l'Oscar pour ce rôle en 2019). Et que Lady Gaga s'avère à la hauteur pour lui donner la réplique. Ça vaut son pesant d'or.

Probably would have faired better in 2022 or so... especially if they had released it a few months after The Batman . However, Hollywood tends to never do what we'd expect. That applies to Warners tenfold. I love bitching about their mishandling of DC in the past 10 years or so. WB deserves to fail, and DC should be in better hands. (End of tangent) Anywho, this Joker sequel is nowhere near as bad as many people made it out to be. I'd argue it's rather brilliant. We see the inner workings of Arthur's fantasies on full display. The tone is even bleaker than the first film; it's riddled with despondency, and oozes onto the viewers. I could quite literally feel the life force being sucked out of me. I swear I couldn't break out of my slump for hours afterward. There's something profound about the musical sequences. Every bit built up to a crescendo of sadness. When the world is so dire, cruel, and unjust – some people who were dealt a bad hand in life, turn into monsters who reflect the state of society. Joker is the persona and mirror image of our corrupt and inverted world. The weight of being the people's conduit for their frustrations in the world eventually broke Arthur, and he was no longer Joker. As he stated, "I can't do this anymore." To make matters extremely worse – Lee didn't truly love the man behind the mask. Only what he managed to stand for. The funny yet sad truth is that oftentimes people do this; they love an idea or aspect about somebody but if it crumbles, they abandon you. Joker 2 is a testament to abandonment. Arthur is the ultimate outcast. A misunderstood man, who knew nothing but trauma and pain most of his life. A mind that attempted to shelter itself from the harsh realities of human nature, and after all that he managed to stand for, during his brief moment in the sun – the world still swallowed him whole.

Shut up all of you. This movie, while definitely not as impactful as the first one, is straight genius 1. The idea of the Joker Arthur Fleck’s death at the end definitely shocked me, but its such a clever take on it. The Joker isnt one singular person, its an idea, a concept, a shared belief. So many people take roles playing the Joker because its not just one person theyre representing. They all have different takes on his quirks, his behaviour, his mental state because theyre taking this concept of the Joker and making it their own. And making this apart of the film’s themes had me gobsmacked 2. The lighting The lighting in both movies is incredible. Unfortunately, i began to conjure up this idea because of a tiktok, but it makes so much sense. Arthur is blue, Joker is yellow… together they make green. Lee is often dressed in yellow, pulling him into the fantasy of “the joker”. And when these different “sides” of him connect (or when he doesnt know which side to believe, the lighting is green. Joker : Folie à Deux est une suite qui prend un chemin très différent du premier film. Plutôt que de simplement reproduire la recette du succès de 2019, le film propose une approche plus psychologique, plus intime et plus expérimentale, en mélangeant drame judiciaire, romance et comédie musicale. J’ai beaucoup aimé retrouver Joaquin Phoenix dans le rôle d’Arthur Fleck. Son interprétation reste impressionnante : il arrive à montrer toute la fragilité, la souffrance et la complexité du personnage. Lady Gaga apporte également une vraie présence dans le rôle d’Harley Quinn, avec une relation entre eux qui oscille entre fascination, amour et manipulation. Les scènes musicales sont intéressantes car elles représentent davantage l’état mental des personnages qu’un simple moment de spectacle. Elles montrent leurs fantasmes, leurs émotions et leur besoin d’échapper à la réalité. La mise en scène reste très travaillée, avec une ambiance sombre et une photographie toujours aussi réussie. Cependant, le film peut sembler long et frustrant pour ceux qui attendaient un thriller plus proche du premier Joker. Le rythme est plus lent, l’histoire avance peu par moments et certains choix artistiques peuvent donner l’impression de prendre de la distance avec ce que les spectateurs avaient aimé dans le premier film. Une suite ambitieuse et différente, qui ne cherche pas à plaire à tout le monde. Portée par de grandes performances et une vraie proposition artistique, mais qui manque parfois de l’impact émotionnel du premier volet.

Do not really get the criticism this film faced when it first came out. This film isn’t meant to be a box standard comic book movie - yet, neither was the first. The film overall is gripping. Given the context of the first, it shows that Arthur has a serious mental illness which has manifested itself in the form of the Joker. The whole film’s plot shows that there is no comic book glamour to mental illness in real life. Arthur is struggling to alongside this personality as it creates delusions of grandeur in order to help Arthur cope with the consequences of his actions in the first film. Overall, this film is about a vulnerable, scared man. A man who has been repeatedly failed by the institutions that are meant to help him in the fist place. The beauty of this film doesn’t come from the “Joker” label that Arthur is trying to push. There’s no realism in having him turn into the character everyone was wanting him to be  The beauty comes from the self awareness of Arthur’s own vulnerability as his delusions crumble around him.
As a cigarette smoker, there are some spectacular smoking scenes, truly a masterpiece of cigarette cinema. As a regular movie watcher, I feel like this could have been an five-episode series.

It is definitely a different beast from its predecessor - more legal drama (albeit with musical interludes) than thriller - in the first couple of acts at least… and the differences in tone can be difficult to get used to. It looks great, there’s some really brilliant shots! The production levels here are genuinely fantastic and from start to finish it is never anything but a joy to look at. And the music choices really worked for me (and I loved hearing a bit of Nick Cave in the opening). I think it is, perhaps, a little muddled in what message it wants to put across, but what you cannot accuse it of is ever trying to play it safe. It takes some swings. Big swings. Bigger swings than Marvel or DC have taken for some time. And I would prefer my films to try something new and daring than just shoving out the same cookie cutter blandness that we so often get. And it’s middle finger to those that misinterpreted- wilfully or otherwise - the first film was welcome.

If the first Joker suffered from being an inferior copy of films made by Murray Franklin's generation (a debt that it tried to diminish by cloaking the slaying of its father figure in an obfuscatory veil of moral outrage), Joker: Folie à Deux finally gives us the artist Todd Phillips lui-même . Sure, Pennies from Heaven and Dancer in the Dark are clear influences on the reality/musical polarity that he is working with, but tonally Folie à Deux is entirely its own beast: the central dichotomy goes far beyond "reality = depressing" and "musical = happy" by making sure that both states feel equally strange and unique. The musical scenes have a twitching, delicate baby-bird awkwardness to them but also a touch of empty dopamine delirium of the kind that a real-life Arthur might escape into on his digital devices, while the "real" scenes are unsettled by Hildur Guðnadóttir's raspy, reptilian soundtrack, often playing underneath songs (both diegetic and non-diegetic) to create the sense of a murderous id straining to emerge from underneath Arthur's sincere romanticism. As for the "message" of the film, there have been too many moronic and reductive takes on it to count, but suffice to say that I've yet to read an analysis that pegs every subtle change of heart the film has about Joker's impending self-renunciation; reviewers have been so eager to paint the film as a critique of the original film and its fans that they have completely missed that Arthur's "apology" turns out to be a disaster on every level, and that it is the premature, irresponsible way that he relinquishes the spotlight that gives birth to the actual Joker of Batman lore. For eighteen years now, film studios have made billions selling superheroes as a soft, infinitely customizable consumerist mythology for specifically the social media generation. Joker: Folie à Deux shows what happens when a director who has zero interest in making back one penny of his budget hijacks this mythology to make something more akin to Babylon or Megalopolis : guess what - for once, those gaudy, plastic mannequins come alive. The archetypes they embody are familiar to us all: here is the ineffectual man identifying with avatars of virile, pornified, video game-ified, meme-ified monstrousness but who actually exists in a mood of chronic limerence emanating from the memory of a single woman who once said something kind to him; there is the glassy-eyed woman in her glass cage of autism/ADHD/CPTSD/therapy/Tinder/doomscrolling but whose mummified face breaks into a healthy smile when she finally encounters something real. The film roots for these broken people, but also lets us know how quickly they will lapse back into their demonic shell-selves when their fragile hopes for something better are shown to be founded on nothing. Ultimately, their folie à deux is the corrupted expression of something good: had they been born in a different milieu, Arthur and Lee's shared dream might not have been so different from Manny's and Nellie's folie à coke room , or Cesar's and Julia's folie à megalon .
